Indexes are scoped per project/worktree, can warm on project open or agent run start, expose progress/health/freshness, handle reindex and teardown, and fall back to deterministic file scan or ripgrep/path search when unavailable, stale, unsupported, disabled, or over budget. Fallback state must be carried to consumers.
gui_classification_reason: Lifecycle and fallback service behavior; not direct GUI/UI/visual presentation work.
negative_constraints: Do not silently return stale results without freshness metadata.
Do not fail an ordinary agent task just because the discovery index is cold when a deterministic fallback can satisfy the request.
Do not leave watchers, database handles, or per-run discovery resources alive after their owning scope is closed.
title: Specify discovery lifecycle, freshness, teardown, and fallback behavior

canonical_summary: First acceptance workflow: when Jared asks an agent to fix a bug without giving an exact path, the agent must invoke DiscoveryService, receive ranked candidates with provenance/freshness/fallback/policy state, read the selected candidate files, verify with exact search/AST/LSP/tests as appropriate, and produce a receipt showing both discovery and verification before editing or claiming the fix target.
gui_classification_reason: Agent validation workflow; not GUI/UI/visual implementation work.
negative_constraints: Do not accept a pass where the agent only uses ripgrep, only uses a GUI picker, or only guesses paths from memory.
Do not accept a pass where the discovery receipt omits freshness/fallback/policy state.
Do not accept a pass where no exact verification occurs before edits.
title: Validate ordinary bug-fix agent discovery workflow

canonical_summary: GUI/agent parity acceptance: the same discovery query, run through Assistant Chat @file or file mention, Planning Wizard context/source picker, PRDBuilder source picker, and an agent discovery tool, should return compatible ordered candidates and the same policy/freshness/fallback semantics for the same project/worktree and permissions context. GUI surfaces should preserve shared ranking order unless they explicitly disclose a user-selected local sort/filter.
gui_classification_reason: This validation criterion directly covers user-visible Assistant Chat, Planning Wizard, PRDBuilder, @file/file mention, picker ordering, and GUI result presentation.
negative_constraints: Do not accept GUI surfaces that re-rank differently without disclosure.
Do not accept agent tools that use a different index or policy envelope than GUI surfaces.
Do not accept parity tests that ignore denied/stale/fallback cases.
title: Validate GUI and agent discovery parity on shared substrate

canonical_summary: Conformance tests should cover every agent-bearing consumer row. Each row should prove the consumer uses DiscoveryService, passes request/policy context, preserves or correctly consumes result order, handles freshness/fallback/denied states, hands off to exact verification when needed, and emits receipts or telemetry sufficient to audit discovery behavior.
gui_classification_reason: The conformance matrix includes GUI consumers as well as agent tools and tests user-visible result ordering semantics, so it is GUI-related.
negative_constraints: Do not accept a consumer row that calls ripgrep or local filesystem scan directly as its primary discovery path while claiming shared discovery support.
Do not accept a row with no denied/fallback/stale case.
Do not require WorkNode creation in this ledger phase; this is future conformance specification only.
title: Validate consumer conformance for shared discovery access

canonical_summary: Before compile, the ledger should lock the scope boundary between file/path discovery and content search. Recommended direction: MVP native discovery is file, directory, mixed path, and context-candidate discovery; content regex search remains owned by Instant Grep / grep / codesearch, with DiscoveryService allowed to provide `content_candidate` hints only as a handoff to exact verification, not as a replacement search backend.

canonical_summary: Before compile, the ledger should include a doc-impact and consumer-impact matrix rather than only owner hints. canonical_summary: Before compile, frecency/query/open history persistence needs privacy and reset semantics. The ledger should define whether history is project-local, user-local, worktree-specific, encrypted or redacted, how long it is retained, whether GUI settings expose reset/disable controls, and whether agents can consume history without surfacing user-private patterns.

negative_constraints: Do not persist query/open history without explicit retention and reset semantics.
Do not expose user-private history patterns to agents without policy rules.
Do not make frecency impossible to disable or clear.

canonical_summary: Before compile, discovery behavior for remote projects, GitHub cache, bare Git content, non-Git projects, multiple worktrees, branch changes, and project path rebinding needs a concrete contract. Existing Instant Grep canon already has remote/cache ownership, so native discovery should either align with those storage and GitHub boundaries or explicitly defer remote discovery as non-MVP.

negative_constraints: Do not assume local filesystem-only behavior if PM's project can be remote or cache-backed.

title: Specify remote, cache, branch, and worktree discovery behavior

canonical_summary: Before compile, performance and resource budgets need enough specificity to validate the native implementation. The ledger should define cold-index, warm-query, reindex, watcher, memory, index-size, cancellation, and timeout expectations, plus observable fallback thresholds for unsupported, stale, disabled, over-budget, or degraded discovery paths.
gui_classification_reason: Runtime performance/resource behavior; not directly GUI/UI/visual presentation work.
negative_constraints: Do not call native discovery successful without measurable latency and resource expectations.
Do not hide over-budget behavior behind generic fallback.
Do not let watchers or indexes run without cancellation and teardown targets.
title: Specify performance/resource budgets and fallback thresholds

canonical_summary: Before compile, GUI discovery states need explicit behavior. Assistant Chat @file/file mentions, Quick Open/command palette, Search path narrowing, File Manager type-ahead, Planning Wizard source/context pickers, and PRDBuilder source picker should specify loading, indexing, stale, fallback, denied, no-results, hidden-by-policy, rank explanation, local sort/filter, and settings/reset states.

negative_constraints: Do not compile GUI consumers with only a backend service reference and no visible state behavior.
Do not show denied or hidden-by-policy paths as ordinary no-results.
Do not allow GUI re-sort/filter to obscure the shared ranking without disclosure.

canonical_summary: Before compile, the no-leak policy should explicitly cover side channels. Discovery must define whether filtering happens before scoring, how denied result counts are suppressed or generalized, how explanations avoid revealing blocked filenames, and how fallback/health diagnostics avoid confirming hidden files, directories, or secret paths.
gui_classification_reason: Security/policy constraint; not directly GUI/UI/visual presentation work.
negative_constraints: Do not leak blocked paths through counts, score explanations, rank gaps, diagnostics, or fallback summaries.
Do not reveal whether a secret path exists by distinguishing denied-hit from no-hit in unauthorized contexts.
Do not let GUI hidden-by-policy labels expose specific blocked path identity.
title: Extend discovery no-leak policy to side channels and diagnostics

canonical_summary: Before compile, ambient agent use needs an explicit tool-selection and receipt contract. Agent prompts, tool routers, Orchestrator, Executor, and WorkNode intake should specify when discovery is attempted, when it is skipped, how fallback is recorded, how exact verification is linked, and how receipts prove discovery was used without making every task noisy or mandatory.

negative_constraints: Do not make ambient discovery an invisible un-auditable habit.

It should cover file, directory, mixed path, symbol-adjacent or context-candidate discovery, and `content_candidate` hints that hand off to Instant Grep, grep, codesearch, AST/LSP, or tests for exact verification.

canonical_summary: Candidate resolution for q-0007: MVP should support full-fidelity local worktree discovery and degraded/read-only path discovery for PM-managed remote or cache-backed projects when a project file manifest or Git cache is already available. Multiple worktrees should be separate index identities. Watchers, low-latency frecency updates, and full freshness guarantees are local-worktree only at MVP; remote/cache results carry explicit cache/fallback freshness state.
gui_classification_reason: Project/cache/worktree discovery behavior; not directly GUI/UI/visual presentation work.
negative_constraints: Do not make remote/cache discovery silently pretend to have local watcher freshness.
Do not merge frecency or index state across worktrees, branches, or project identities.
Do not defer all remote/cache discovery if PM already has a safe manifest/cache source for path discovery.
title: Candidate: local full fidelity plus degraded remote/cache path discovery

canonical_summary: Candidate resolution for q-0008: frecency/query/open history should be on-device, user-scoped, project/worktree-local by default, with visible GUI reset and disable controls. Agents may consume ranking effects and sanitized score breakdowns but should not receive raw private query/open history unless an explicit policy allows it. Privacy or restricted modes can disable history while preserving fuzzy/path ranking.
gui_classification_reason: This specifies visible GUI reset/disable controls and user-facing privacy settings, so it is GUI-related.
negative_constraints: Do not persist frecency history globally across unrelated projects by default.
Do not expose raw user query/open history to agents as ordinary prompt context.
Do not make frecency impossible to reset or disable from the GUI.
title: Candidate: project-local frecency with GUI reset/disable and sanitized agent use

canonical_summary: Candidate resolution for q-0009: use `DiscoveryService` as the internal shared substrate and introduce an explicit agent-facing discovery operation, preferably `discover_paths`, with target_kind values for file, directory, mixed, and context_candidate. Keep grep/codesearch as content-search tools. Use discovery-specific receipts/events such as `discovery.invoked`, `discovery.candidates_returned`, `discovery.selected`, `discovery.fallback`, and `discovery.verified`, while existing GUI commands may route through DiscoveryService without being renamed.

Do not blur path discovery receipts with grep/codesearch verification receipts.
title: Candidate: DiscoveryService plus discover_paths and discovery-specific receipts

canonical_summary: Assistant Chat GUI must show what native discovery is doing inside Assistant Chat threads. When an agent uses discovery, the thread should display user-visible activity for discovery start, index warmup or readiness, candidate ranking, fallback/degraded path, denied or hidden-by-policy outcomes, selected candidate handoff, and exact verification follow-up.
gui_classification_reason: This is directly about visible Assistant Chat thread UI/activity presentation.
negative_constraints: Do not hide discovery behavior only in backend logs or post-run artifacts.

title: Show discovery activity inside Assistant Chat threads

canonical_summary: Assistant Chat visibility acceptance: in the ordinary bug-fix workflow with no exact path, the Assistant Chat thread must show a discovery activity sequence such as discovering project files, warming or checking the index, ranking candidates, using fallback if needed, selecting/reading candidates, and verifying with grep/codesearch/AST/LSP/tests before edits. The thread must distinguish no results, stale/fallback, denied, hidden-by-policy, and exact-path skip states without leaking blocked paths.
gui_classification_reason: This validation criterion directly tests Assistant Chat thread UI/activity behavior.
negative_constraints: Do not accept a GUI pass where discovery is only visible in a final receipt.

title: Validate Assistant Chat discovery activity visibility
